judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whereas clauses pile up sweeping purpose language ('greatest benefits', 'most efficient service in the public welfare') and open-ended lists of goals whose boundaries are undefined. As pure recitals they create no operative duty, but their generality invites argument about the scope of the agency's mission.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These recitals describe a broad basin-wide regulatory mission that parties would use to expand or narrow operative terms such as the Section 1.2(g) definition of 'project' and Section 3.8's referral requirement, a classic recital-versus-operative tension. That makes them a likely interpretive battleground even though they impose nothing themselves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short-title clause with a stray double period ('Short title..'); the typo does not change meaning. Nothing here is capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'this Act' while Section 1.2(c) defines 'Compact' as only Part I of the act, a mild definitional mismatch. The mismatch has no practical consequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out 'except as may be otherwise required by the context' makes every defined term defeasible without saying when, which is itself an open-ended standard. That phrase is the only construable feature.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matters because it lets a party argue the Section 1.2(g) 'project' definition yields to context in Section 3.8 or Article 11, so it is bound up with the compact's central interpretive fight. Standing alone, though, it conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Area of drainage into the Delaware River and its tributaries, including Delaware Bay' is a hydrologically determinate boundary. No term is genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section 2.7 (jurisdiction within the basin) and Article 10 without strain. No conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure naming definition with a single referent. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.1 creating the commission. No tension anywhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Part I of this act' is precise, though 'this act' shifts referent depending on which sovereign's enactment is read. That is a slight but real indeterminacy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Part II contains five different enacting statutes (federal Section 15.1, Delaware, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania), so 'this act' has five candidates. The effect is minor because the Compact text is identical in each.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net induced adverse effects, whether or not compensated for' is a genuinely vague cost component with no measurement rule. 'Direct and indirect expenditures' compounds the openness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Sections 11.4 and 13.3 on cost allocation, which prescribe no method either, so the vagueness is not cured elsewhere. No direct contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Facility' is defined by an enormous open list closing with 'any and all things and appurtenances necessary, useful or convenient' and 'to facilitate any other uses of any of them' — a textbook general-catch-all-against-specifics problem. Its outer boundary cannot be stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Section 1.2(g) definition of 'project' incorporates 'any separate facility', so the reach of this definition directly controls the compact's central regulatory trigger in Section 3.8. Any fight over what counts as a regulated project runs through this text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any appropriate branch, department, bureau or division thereof, as the case may be' is loose but functionally harmless. 'Appropriate' is the only soft word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Section 1.2(h) making the federal government a signatory party and with the Section 15.1 federal reservations. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Project' means 'any work, service or activity ... for the conservation, utilization, control, development or management of water resources', with modifying clauses whose antecedents ('which can be established and utilized independently') are grammatically unmoored — the definition is both syntactically tangled and substantively boundless. Whether a private activity that merely uses or affects water falls inside it is genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This definition is the trigger for Section 3.8's approval requirement and for Articles 4 through 11, and reading it broadly would swallow Sections 11.1(c) and 11.2(c) preserving existing agency authority and Section 1.3(e)'s promise to 'make secure and protect present developments'. It is the provision on which the whole instrument's coherence turns.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed enumeration of who is a signatory party. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble's list of parties and with Section 14.22. No tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Water resources' sweeps in 'related natural resources in, on, under, or above the ground, including related uses of land' — 'related' is unbounded and does the whole work. Whether subsurface minerals or land uses are 'related natural resources' is squarely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Section 3.8 conditions review on 'substantial effect on the water resources of the basin' and Section 1.2(g) defines projects by reference to water resources, this definition's breadth determines the commission's regulatory reach and its fit with Sections 11.1(c)/11.2(c) and 14.19.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory phrase to legislative findings. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Serves only to introduce 1.3(a)-(e). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A declaratory finding that water resources are 'affected with a ... national interest' and their management is a 'public purpose'; hortatory rather than operative. No named term is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As a finding it could be marshalled against operative limits such as Sections 11.1(c), 11.2(c) and 14.19, a recital-versus-operative risk, but it does not contradict them outright.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States a purpose of 'joint exercise of such powers of sovereignty'; abstract but not two-sided in any operative way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 1.4's reservation of congressional power and Section 5.5's reservation of state authority without contradiction. Only mild recital tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A single administrative agency is therefore essential' is a finding, not a grant; 'essential' is rhetorical. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits awkwardly beside Section 1.5's direction to preserve existing agencies and Sections 11.1(c)/11.2(c), which contemplate continuing parallel authority — a recital pulling against operative text. The tension is real but soft.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The finding that the basin's waters 'are ample to meet all presently projected demands' is a factual assertion with a run-on second half lacking punctuation. Its wording is loose rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits oddly against Article 10, which presupposes water shortages, protected areas and supply emergencies, and against Section 3.3's emergency allocation power. That is a genuine recital-versus-operative mismatch, though unlikely to be litigated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The purpose list includes 'to make secure and protect present developments within the states' and 'equal and uniform treatment to all water users who are similarly situated' — open-ended standards a party could deploy against regulation. 'Present developments' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against the commission's expansive project-review power under Sections 1.2(g) and 3.8 and would be used to argue existing private activities are protected, a recital-versus-operative conflict of exactly the kind courts construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A savings clause preserving congressional powers; standard and reasonably precise. 'In derogation of' is settled usage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(t) makes the United States' membership contingent on this very section surviving constitutional challenge, and Sections 11.1 and 15.1(s) are expressly subordinated to it, so it is a hub of cross-references. Those references are consistent rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent not inconsistent with the compact' and 'to the fullest extent it finds feasible and advantageous' are elastic, self-judging standards. 'Feasible and advantageous' is committed to the commission's own view.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 7.4(b) and 8.2(b) expressly invoke this section's 'intent and purpose' as an operating constraint, so its vagueness propagates. It does not contradict them, but it supplies no workable measure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The renewal window — notice 'not later than 20 years nor sooner than 25 years prior to the termination' — is expressed in a confusing inverted form that reads at first as impossible, and the double negative ('if ... none of the signatory states ... notifies') compounds it. That is a genuine mechanical/drafting defect even if a court could untangle it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the compact addresses termination timing; Section 1.6(b) simply follows on. No conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Says the compact is 'terminated by operation of paragraph (a)' when paragraph (a) actually terminates by state notice, a small mislabel. Winding up is left entirely to Congress, which is definite if one-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives Congress alone the wind-up power although the states are the parties who can terminate under 1.6(a) and Section 14.20 requires unanimity to amend — a modest structural oddity. Not a squarely conflicting provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward creation clause; 'body politic and corporate' is a term of art. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.1 (corporate powers) and 15.1(m) (not a federal agency). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is clear on its face: the federal commissioner serves 'during the term of office of the President'. No internal ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The compact's own endnote states that Sections 2.2 and 15.1(d) 'were inconsistent as to the term of the federal representative's appointment' — 15.1(d) says the member serves at the President's pleasure — a conflict acknowledged in the instrument itself and cured only by later federal legislation. That is a documented Category 2.1 defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear appointment, tenure and vacancy mechanics; 'in his place and stead' is conventional. Nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(d) overrides the tenure rule for the federal alternate and the endnote records the resulting inconsistency, so this section too was affected. The override is expressed as a 'notwithstanding', which largely harmonises it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for necessary expenses' is a clean rule; 'necessary' is the only soft word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) provides that 'the provisions of Sections 2.4 and 2.6 ... notwithstanding' the federal member and advisor may be paid compensation by the United States — a direct, if expressly reconciled, contradiction of the no-compensation rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A majority of the membership' is determinate given a fixed five-member body. The rule is stated crisply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.3(a) and 13.3(b)(2) require unanimity for particular actions and Section 14.5(a) speaks of 'a majority of the full membership', so the general rule yields in places; these are express exceptions rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Routine internal-organisation provision with a discretionary advisor appointment. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) expressly qualifies Section 2.6 as to advisor compensation and New York Section 632 designates the advisor, both consistent overlays. No genuine conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or convenient to effectuate its powers or duties within the basin' is an elastic extraterritorial trigger, and the final consent sentence's 'such power' has an uncertain antecedent. There is something here to argue about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with Section 1.2(e), which contemplates facilities 'within or without the basin', so the two are consistent; the consent requirement is not repeated elsewhere. No square conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad mandatory language ('shall develop and effectuate plans, policies and projects') without limits, but it is a policy statement rather than a rule with edges. Little specific ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates powers detailed in Articles 3 and 13 and is consistent with them. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare directive to formulate three documents in accordance with Article 13. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a cross-referencing duplicate of Article 13; the substantive terms differ slightly between the two, but this stem does not.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: a comprehensive plan after consultation with water users and public bodies. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.1 states the same duty with additional consultation requirements (public utilities, public hearings), so the two must be read together; the overlap is cumulative, not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such reasonably foreseeable period as the commission may determine' is self-defining and open-ended, and the sentence is a single long clause. Mild vagueness only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.2 fixes the same program at 'the ensuing six years or such other reasonably foreseeable period', so the two provisions state the horizon differently — a small inconsistency between duplicative texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires two budgets 'consistent with the water resources program'; definite. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.3 elaborates the same budgets consistently. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In accordance with the doctrine of equitable apportionment' imports an inherently indeterminate legal standard, and 'from time to time as need appears' is equally soft. Those are namable open terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly cabined by 3.3(a)-(c), Section 3.4 and Section 3.5, and paragraph (b) then says allocations are not an apportionment — a notable tension with the equitable-apportionment premise of this stem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and conditional but internally coherent; 'state of emergency resulting from a drought or catastrophe' is broad yet workable. Only 'catastrophe' is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Sections 3.4 and 3.5 which protect the same 1954 decree, and with Section 10.4's separate emergency machinery requiring only commission action rather than unanimity — a possible overlap in emergency authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Denies allocations any priority or apportionment effect, then adds a proviso preserving covenant power; the proviso partly undercuts the rule. 'Apportionment' bears a technical meaning that sits oddly with the section's own equitable-apportionment reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3's stem directs allocation 'in accordance with the doctrine of equitable apportionment' while this paragraph says no allocation 'shall be deemed to constitute an apportionment' — a genuine internal pull within the same section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any proper party deeming itself aggrieved' is undefined, and 'court of competent jurisdiction' is left unspecified in the compact itself. Both are namable soft terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York Section 634 supplies a state-specific meaning for 'court of competent jurisdiction' and Section 15.1(p) gives federal district courts original jurisdiction, so the phrase draws meaning from outside this section. Those overlays are complementary rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense waiver with two nested exceptions and a cross-reference to unquoted decree paragraphs 'IIIB3 and VB', which cannot be applied without the external decree. The double 'increase or decrease' phrasing is confusing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Sections 3.3(a) and 3.5, which also preserve the decree; Section 3.5 says 'except as specifically provided in Sections 3.3 and 3.4', so the three must be harmonised. They can be, but only with effort.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A savings clause with 'to this end, and without limitation thereto' followed by four specific prohibitions; the general-then-specific structure invites ejusdem generis argument. The prohibitions themselves are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly excepts Sections 3.3 and 3.4 and thus depends on their scope; Section 3.8 is also made 'subject to' it. The cross-references are coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Impede or interfere with' is a broad, unquantified prohibition covering any 'order or action'. That breadth is arguable but the direction is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It could bar commission action otherwise authorised by Sections 3.6(a) and 4.1, but the compact resolves that by making those powers subject to Section 3.5. The hierarchy is stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat prohibition on fees for decree-permitted diversions; short and definite. Nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.7 grants a broad rate-setting power and Section 15.1(b) adds a further federal restriction on it, so three provisions govern charges; the carve-outs are expressed as limits and can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but structured; the consent requirement and the scope of covered structures are stated. 'Used in connection with' is the only elastic phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts the Section 3.8 approval power over decree-related facilities, which Section 3.8 expressly acknowledges by being 'subject to the provisions of Sections 3.3 and 3.5'. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, one prohibition, one exception. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Section 3.3(a)'s reference to consulting the river master. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-word permissive stem. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Introduces powers that are elsewhere cabined by Sections 3.5 and 11; the stem itself creates no tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A very long verb list ending in 'determined by the commission to be necessary, convenient or useful for the purposes of this compact' — a self-judging standard, but the drafting is deliberate. Some open texture, little true ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 7.4(b) and 8.2(b) forbid the commission from operating projects where another agency is available, and Section 1.5 directs use of existing agencies, so this broad power is qualified elsewhere. The qualifications are express.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All projects and facilities in the basin which affect its water resources, including without limitation thereto' a specific list — the enumerated items are far narrower than the general grant, raising a classic list-scope question. 'Affect' is unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: By contrast Section 3.8 requires only projects with a 'substantial effect' to be submitted, so the two provisions use different effect thresholds for overlapping subject matter. That mismatch is worth noting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A research and data power with an illustrative list introduced by 'without limitation thereto'. Broad but not contested territory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(d), 3.6(e) and 13.1. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For water uses, flood warning, quality maintenance or other purposes' ends a short list with an unbounded catch-all. That is a minor ejusdem generis point in a purely permissive clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 6.4's warning and posting power without contradicting it. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Narrow, purposive and tied to the comprehensive plan. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Sections 13.1 and 3.6(c). No tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A publication power stated plainly. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.12's reporting duty. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As the commission may deem necessary or desirable' is self-judging, but the clause is a routine funding power. Little to fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 12.20(c) and 14.13 cover the same receipt-of-funds ground consistently. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such other and different powers ... and ... all powers necessary or convenient to carry out its express powers or which may be reasonably implied therefrom' is a residual catch-all sitting at the end of an enumerated list — the paradigm general-versus-specific problem. Its reach is precisely what a party would dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read broadly it would let the commission escape the specific limits in Sections 3.5, 7.4(b), 8.2(b), 11.1(c) and 11.2(c), so its scope cannot be settled without harmonising the whole instrument. That is a live whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grants rate-fixing 'for the use of facilities which it may own or operate', which is a stated limit; 'without regulation or control by any ... agency of any signatory party' is emphatic but clear. Modest ambiguity only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(b) expressly provides that 'no provision of Section 3.7 ... shall be deemed to authorize' charges on pre-existing withdrawals or on navigation, and Section 3.5(b) bars fees on decree diversions, so this grant is contradicted in part by two other operative provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger — 'no project having a substantial effect on the water resources of the basin' undertaken 'by any person, corporation or governmental authority' — turns on the undefined intensity word 'substantial' and on the contested defined term 'project'. Both the threshold and the class of regulated actors are open on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope depends entirely on Section 1.2(g)'s definition of 'project' and Section 1.2(i)'s 'water resources', and a broad reading collides with Sections 11.1(c) and 11.2(c) preserving other agencies' authority and with Section 1.3(e)'s protection of 'present developments'. This is the provision through which the whole compact's coherence must be tested.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text reads 'To this end, but with limitation thereto, the commission may' — plainly a mechanical error for 'without limitation thereto', and the error reverses the meaning from illustrative to exhaustive. That is a Category 1.2 defect on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel provisions (Sections 3.5, 4.1, 3.6(b), 3.6(c)) all use 'without limitation thereto', confirming the mistake and creating a mismatch in how the compact frames its enumerations. Whether paragraphs (a)-(d) are exhaustive turns on that comparison.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short cooperation power with familiar verbs. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 11.5 and 14.1(a)(1). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ends with 'or for any other purpose', an unbounded catch-all after a specific list of engineering functions. That is a small list-scope point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Section 1.5's direction to employ existing agencies. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'So far as consistent with the comprehensive plan' is a workable qualifier; 'permit the decentralized administration thereof' is vague but permissive. Limited scope for dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Sections 13.1 and 1.5. No conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, concrete qualification power. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(g) and 12.20(c). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive power to constitute advisory committees with an illustrative membership list. Nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Section 2.6's advisor provision and New York Section 632's advisory committee. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To this end, without limitation thereto' opens an expansive list of construction powers and 'such off-river sites as it may find appropriate' is self-judging. Broad but purposive drafting rather than ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.5 then denies power 'to engage in the business of distributing water', which cuts back the broad grant here; the line between the two is not drawn. That interaction is the main risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of purposes ends with 'the prevention of undue salinity and other purposes' — an unbounded catch-all after specifics, and 'undue' is itself a soft word. Both are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Sections 5.1, 6.1 and 9.1 without contradicting any of them. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No signatory party shall permit any augmentation of flow to be diminished by the diversion of any water' is a convoluted double-negative obligation whose subject (what a party must prevent, and by whom) is not crisp. The exceptions are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Sections 3.3 and 3.5 protecting decree diversions and with Article 10's permit regime; the exception for diversions 'duly authorized by this compact' does that work. Broadly harmonisable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Specially benefited thereby to a measurable extent' and 'no such assessment shall exceed the actual benefit to any water user' set standards that cannot be applied without a valuation method. 'Actual benefit' is the contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.5(b) forbids charges on decree-permitted diversions and Section 15.1(b) restricts charges on pre-existing withdrawals, so the assessment power collides at the edges with those limits, which this section does not mention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear procedural condition: review existing rights and hold a public hearing before executing an Article 4 project. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.4(b) sets the general hearing procedure and this adds a project-specific hearing; consistent. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Engage in the business of distributing water' is an undefined boundary between permitted transmission facilities and prohibited distribution. That line is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1 grants sweeping power to construct and operate water-supply facilities and Section 2.7 permits sale of water, so this prohibition constrains grants stated elsewhere without defining where. The tension is real but modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward pollution-control powers plus a right to invoke state agencies as complainant. No ambiguous term stands out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 5.2 and 5.4 supply the regulatory and enforcement machinery, and Section 5.5 preserves state authority; all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The controlling standard — pollution 'shall not injuriously affect waters of the basin as contemplated by the comprehensive plan' — is doubly indeterminate, and 'assume jurisdiction' is undefined. 'Injuriously affect' is the namable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 preserves stricter state legislation and Section 15.1(k) preserves federal water-pollution functions, so three regimes overlap; those provisions expressly accommodate each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A covenant to 'enact any necessary legislation' to achieve descriptive water-quality goals ('free from unsightly or malodorous nuisances') that are aesthetic and unmeasurable. Those adjectives are genuinely vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It obliges signatory legislatures while Section 5.5 preserves their freedom and Section 15.1(k) protects federal functions; the covenant's enforceability against sovereign legislatures is left unaddressed anywhere in the compact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed enforcement provision with clear procedural steps. 'Court of competent jurisdiction' is undefined but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York Section 634 defines that phrase for that state and Section 15.1(p) gives federal courts original jurisdiction, so the forum question is answered elsewhere. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short savings clause preserving state anti-pollution authority; direction is plain. 'Additional conditions and restrictions' is the only soft phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 10.8, which supersedes conflicting state permits, and Section 14.2's compact-wide regulatory power, so state authority is preserved in Article 5 but overridden in Article 10 — an asymmetry a party could exploit. Still largely reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As it may deem necessary or desirable' and 'as the commission may deem appropriate' are self-judging but the subject matter is narrow. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.2(a) and 6.2. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Recommended standards' is an odd hybrid — the commission may 'adopt, amend and repeal' them, yet they are only recommended, leaving their legal force unclear. That is a namable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.3 requires acquisitions to 'be in accord with the standards adopted and promulgated pursuant to Section 6.2', which treats the same standards as operative rather than merely recommended. That is a genuine internal mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed procedural provision with hearings and availability of proposed standards; 'in the manner provided by Article 14' is a precise cross-reference. Little ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.4(b) supplies the hearing procedure referenced, and New York Section 636 implements the municipal-aid power, both consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unwarranted constrictions' is an unmeasured term, but the acquisition purposes are otherwise concrete. Limited exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires accord with Section 6.2 standards, which are labelled merely 'recommended' — the same mismatch flagged at 6.2(a). Otherwise consistent with Section 14.14's condemnation power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive posting and notice power; 'as conditions may warrant' is soft but consequence-free. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps Section 3.6(d)'s publicity power without contradiction. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall promote sound practices' is hortatory and unenforceable in its terms. Vague but creates no operative boundary to dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 7's later sections supply the concrete powers; consistent. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive power over soil, erosion, reclamation and forestry projects, stated plainly. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subject to Section 7.4(b)'s operating restriction, which is expressly stated. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Narrow permissive power tied to 'water resources of the basin'. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.2(i) and Section 7.4(b). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cooperation duty in one sentence. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Section 8.2(a) verbatim for Article 8; consistent duplication. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No other suitable unit or agency of government is available to operate the same upon reasonable conditions' turns on two undefined standards, 'suitable' and 'reasonable conditions'. Those are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts the sweeping operating power granted by Section 3.6(a) and invokes Section 1.5's equally elastic 'fullest extent it finds feasible and advantageous', so the constraint's force depends on provisions that do not fix it. Genuine but unlikely to be litigated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Water related public sports and recreational facilities' is a slightly loose class but the duty is plain. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly made subject to Section 8.2, and Section 15.1(l) limits Section 8.4's application to federally operated facilities; both accommodations are stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-sentence cooperation duty. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to Section 7.4(a); consistent. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same 'suitable ... upon reasonable conditions' standard as Section 7.4(b), undefined in both. The terms are namable but low-stakes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts back Sections 3.6(a) and 8.1 and depends on Section 1.5's elastic purpose statement, the same interlock noted at 7.4(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within limits prescribed by this article' introduces three duties; the phrase is a cross-reference rather than a standard. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'limits prescribed by this article' presumably means Sections 8.2 and 8.4; the reference is imprecise but harmless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short encouragement and coordination duty. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.9. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Contrast with Section 6.2's 'recommended standards' that Section 6.3 treats as binding; here nothing else gives them force. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Owned or controlled by the commission' and 'in accordance with this article' are definite. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Points to Section 8.4's concession-bidding regime, which Section 15.1(l) then disapplies to federally operated facilities; the interlock is expressly handled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mandates sealed competitive bidding for concessions 'including any renewal or extension thereof'; 'therefore' is a misspelling of 'therefor' that changes nothing. The rule itself is rigid and clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May be impounded and used by or under authority of the commission ... in accordance with the comprehensive plan' is a clear authorisation. No contested term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with Sections 9.2-9.4 and Section 3.5's decree protections; consistent. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain permissive power over dams and generation facilities. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.1 and 9.4. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits transmission facilities 'where such facilities are not otherwise available upon reasonable terms' and 'for the purpose of wholesale marketing', then bars 'direct sale to consumers' — the wholesale/retail boundary and 'reasonable terms' are both open. Namable ambiguities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.7 authorises the commission to 'sell or dispose of ... hydroelectric power' generally, without the retail restriction stated here, so the two grants are stated at different breadths. That is a modest inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Contracts on reasonable terms, consideration and duration' is a soft standard but limited in consequence. Little to fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.2 and 14.4(b)'s hearing requirement. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable, nondiscriminatory, and just' is a classic open standard, though familiar in utility regulation. The terms are namable but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.7 lets the commission fix rates 'without regulation or control by any ... agency of any signatory party', leaving unclear who enforces this reasonableness standard. That gap is a mild whole-instrument issue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such power or regulation or control' appears to be a mechanical error for 'such power of regulation or control', and the delegation power is otherwise open-ended. The typo is visible on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York Section 637 restricts acceptance of delegations to bodies that would otherwise have such power, and Section 10.8 supersedes conflicting state permits, so the delegation scheme depends on outside provisions. Broadly consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Threaten to develop to such a degree as to create a water shortage' is a predictive, unquantified trigger. That standard is namable but committed to the commission.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Sections 10.3, 10.5 and 10.6 coherently. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii) grandfathers permits 'heretofore granted under the laws of any of the signatory states' with no time or scope limit, and the enumerated uses ('domestic, municipal, agricultural or industrial') may or may not be exhaustive. Both are arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.8 says state-issued diversion permits 'shall be superseded to the extent of any conflict' whenever the commission exercises Article 10 powers, which pulls directly against this grandfather clause. That is a real internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Drought or other condition which may cause an actual and immediate shortage' pairs a specific with a general catch-all, and the emergency's duration is set by the commission alone. The catch-all is namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3(a) creates a separate emergency mechanism requiring unanimous consent and consultation with the river master, so two emergency regimes coexist with different procedures. They can be read as covering different subjects, but the overlap is untidy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Just and equitable interests and rights of other lawful users' and 'due regard to the need to balance and reconcile alternative and conflicting uses' are pure standards with no decision rule. Squarely vague terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.6 makes these determinations judicially reviewable without supplying any more concrete criterion, so the vagueness is not cured. No direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sections 10.3 through 10.5' and 'court of competent jurisdiction' are precise enough; the section is short and mechanical. Nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York Section 634 specifies that for that state this phrase means an Article 78 proceeding, and Section 15.1(p) confers federal district court jurisdiction; complementary rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A record-keeping duty on states, defined by what the commission prescribes. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 10.3 and 14.2. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whenever the commission finds it necessary or desirable' is self-judging and 'superseded to the extent of any conflict' leaves the supersession boundary undefined. Both terms are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Section 10.3(ii)'s express preservation of permits 'heretofore granted under the laws of any of the signatory states', and sits uneasily with Section 5.5's savings clause for state authority. That is a specific internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A framing sentence subjecting the following rules to Section 1.4. Nothing to construe on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The subordination to Section 1.4 and the further federal reservations in Section 15.1(s) largely neutralise paragraphs (a)-(c), which is itself a structural tension worth noting. The stem, though, states the hierarchy plainly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All projects related to powers delegated to the commission' uses the contested term 'project' plus the vague connector 'related to'. Consultation itself is a soft obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach depends on Section 1.2(g)'s definition of 'project', and Section 11.1(c) preserves each federal agency's own authority, so the consultation duty's bite is contested by neighbouring text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No expenditure or commitment shall be made ... nor shall it be deemed authorized, unless it shall have first been included by the commission in the comprehensive plan' is an absolute bar on federal spending expressed in sweeping terms. judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to reconcile with Section 11.1(c) (federal agencies 'shall continue to have, exercise and discharge such authority'), with Section 1.4's reservation of congressional power, and with Section 15.1(s)'s presidential override, all of which point the other way. That is a genuine whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as specifically provided by this section' is a narrow carve-out but its interaction with the absolute bar in (b) is not spelled out. The exception's scope is the arguable point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph (b) prohibits any federal expenditure not in the comprehensive plan while this paragraph preserves each agency's full authority, and Section 15.1(s) adds a presidential power to delete plan provisions — the three cannot be squared without reading one down.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A framing sentence for state and local project rules. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Section 11.1 but omits the 'subject to Section 1.4' qualifier, an asymmetry that is deliberate rather than defective.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same 'projects related to powers delegated' formula as Section 11.1(a), depending on the contested term 'project'. Consultation is otherwise a soft duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope is set by Section 1.2(g) and it must live alongside Section 11.2(c)'s preservation of state and local authority. Modest tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An absolute prohibition on state and local expenditure for any project not first included in the comprehensive plan, with no de minimis threshold. Its breadth against ordinary municipal works is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts in direction with Section 11.2(c)'s preservation of state and local authority and with Section 3.8, which conditions review on a project having a 'substantial effect' — this paragraph has no such threshold. That mismatch is a concrete incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as specifically provided by this section' preserves existing authority in terms whose interaction with (b) is unstated. The carve-out's reach is the contestable point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with paragraph (b)'s blanket bar and with Section 3.8's substantial-effect threshold, the compact says both that state agencies keep their powers and that they may spend nothing outside the plan. Harmonising the two requires reading one down.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short reservation of state taxing power over withdrawals; the terms 'fees, charges and taxes' are broad but clear in direction. Little ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.7 lets the commission fix charges 'without regulation or control by any ... agency of any signatory party' and Section 14.3 exempts the commission from state taxation, so overlapping charges on the same water are contemplated without a priority rule. A modest gap rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A duty to establish uniform standards and 'equitable cost sharing and reimbursement formulas'; 'equitable' is soft but the obligation is procedural. Limited exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports Sections 12.20(a) and 13.3's apportionment machinery, and the 2007 and 2014 federal amendments in the Endnote address 'equitable funding requirements' consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single itemised requirement for cost-allocation procedures. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.2(d) and 13.3. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list item about contracts and supervision of performance; plainly stated. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 12.20(a). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An accounting-system item, entirely mechanical. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.11's audit regime. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Directs apportionment of reimbursable revenues and payments in lieu of taxes; concrete. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.3 already fixes a ten-year in-lieu payment formula for property taxes, so this item's discretion overlaps a prescribed rule. Minor duplication rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Pledges itself to provide technical and administrative services ... within the limits of available appropriations' is a promise that its own qualifier can hollow out. That self-cancelling structure is namable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section says bonds are 'payable solely out of the properties and revenues of the commission without recourse to taxation' and in the next breath that 'the full faith and credit of the commission are hereby pledged' — those two characterisations sit awkwardly together within one provision. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.3 denies any power to pledge signatory credit while Section 12.20(b) contemplates signatory guarantees of the same bonds, so the security architecture is stated inconsistently across the article.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The purpose of this compact shall include without limitation thereto all costs of any project or facility' is a mechanical error — a cost-eligibility list has been mislabelled as a statement of the compact's purpose. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.1 authorises borrowing 'for any of the purposes of this compact' and Section 1.3(e) states those purposes quite differently, so this section's misuse of 'purpose' cannot be reconciled with either without rewriting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear negative covenant plus a personal-liability shield. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.20(b) allows signatory guarantees of commission bonds, which is at least in tension with the flat denial of power to impose payment obligations on a signatory. The guarantee provision's 'notwithstanding any other provision' language largely resolves it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed refunding machinery, precisely drafted. Nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.5 and 12.13. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard bond-authorisation provisions with clear validity savings. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.6, 12.13 and 12.16. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very long but conventional indenture-covenant enumeration; the exclusion of 'any restriction on the regulatory powers vested in the commission' is a clear limit. Little ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.18's trust-fund restriction on revenues and Section 3.7's rate power both interact with the covenants contemplated here; the carve-out for regulatory powers keeps them consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No bond or its terms shall mature in more than fifty years from its own date' is awkwardly worded — a bond's 'terms' do not mature — but the fifty-year limit is unmistakable. A cosmetic rather than meaning-changing slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 1.6(a)'s hundred-year compact duration and Section 12.4's refunding power without difficulty. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Exempts bonds from 'all taxation by or under authority of any of the signatory parties, except for transfer, inheritance and estate taxes' — clear on its face. The exception list is closed and specific.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence leaving the rate entirely to the commission; 'payable annually or semi-annually' is a closed choice. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise administrative power over place and currency of payment. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.6 and 12.11. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Facsimile signature and surviving-signature rules stated with precision. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.5 and 12.6. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires sale 'on sealed proposals to the highest bidder' yet then permits private sale after rejection of bids, and defines the limit by 'net interest cost' rather than price — the highest-bidder rule and the interest-cost ceiling are two different yardsticks in one provision. judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line negotiability rule with a clear exception. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.5 and 12.6 on registered form. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Declares bonds legal investments for named classes; concrete. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applies only 'in each of the signatory states', leaving federal fiduciaries unaddressed even though the United States is a signatory party under Section 1.2(h). A small definitional gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Conclusive against all persons whomsoever' is sweeping but unmistakable in meaning. Nothing genuinely two-sided.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recording, effectiveness and delivery rules stated plainly. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.6 and 12.18. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section 12.6's covenant powers and Section 3.7's rate-setting power over the same revenues; those are complementary rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A structured remedies clause closing with an express non-exclusivity sentence, which forecloses the usual expressio unius argument. Well drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Court of competent jurisdiction of any signatory party' is qualified by Section 15.1(p) and New York Section 634, and Section 12.3 bars personal liability; all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad permissive funding provision with plain terms. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Sections 3.6(g) and 14.13 consistently. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The ensuing six years or such other reasonably foreseeable period as the commission may determine' lets the commission displace the stated period at will, which is a namable soft term. Otherwise the duty is clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line content requirement. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 3.2(b). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.2(c) and 12.20(a). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive stem introducing corporate powers. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.1's creation of a body corporate. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains the obvious typographical error 'enter intro contracts' for 'into contracts'; the slip is visible but does not alter the evident meaning. A mechanical defect of the mildest kind.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Sue and be sued in all courts of competent jurisdiction' interacts with Section 15.1(p) and New York Section 634, which define the forum; also with Section 15.1(p)'s preservation of United States immunity. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but plainly worded power to receive funds and property. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Sections 3.6(g), 12.20(c) and 14.13. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A planning and specification power tied to 'any facility or project', both defined terms. No ambiguity of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach follows Sections 1.2(e) and 1.2(g), whose breadth is contested, but this clause adds nothing controversial.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short control power over the commission's own facilities. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.7 and 14.2(a). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long verb and method lists ending with 'or otherwise as it may deem necessary' and 'necessary, useful or convenient' — general catch-alls after specifics, though in a purely enabling clause. Mild list-scope exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.14's condemnation power and Section 12.18's restrictions on disposing of pledged facilities both bear on the same subject; they qualify rather than contradict this grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stem subjecting the commissioners' functions to the compact. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to any provisions of law specifically applicable to agencies or instrumentalities created by compact' points at an undefined body of law. That reference is vague but consequential only at the margin.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short internal-administration duty. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.6. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad personnel power qualified by 'subject to the provisions of this article'. Nothing genuinely two-sided.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line contracting power. Nothing indeterminate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-word permissive stem. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Vesting commission employees with 'the powers of a peace officer of the state' is a striking grant whose content depends entirely on unspecified state law. The scope of those powers is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.17 leaves penal sanctions to signatory-state statutes and Section 15.1(m) denies federal agency status, so enforcement authority is distributed across sovereigns without a coordinating rule. That is a structural loose end rather than a flat conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All meetings of the commission shall be open to the public' is absolute and unqualified — no exception for deliberation, personnel or litigation matters. The absence of exceptions is itself a construable feature.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed notice-and-hearing rule with a closed list plus 'all other cases wherein this compact requires a public hearing'. The catch-all points to identifiable sections rather than being open-ended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single public-records sentence. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Solely on the basis of merit and fitness' and 'found by the commission to be guilty of a violation' are broad, and removal is mandatory with no procedure specified. Namable but conventional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear oath requirement with a fixed deadline. Nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stem introducing three prohibitions. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.8(b)-(d). No conflict.
